Paper_Metadata.Paper_Title: Phase formation capability and compositional design of β-phase multiple rare-earth principal component disilicates

Composition_Info.Note: Nominal equimolar four-RE principal-component disilicate. The paper states homogeneous RE distribution and pure single-phase β solid solution for the as-synthesized powder, but no full overall measured elemental normalization was reported for the powder.

Process_Text.original: Commercial rare-earth oxides and SiO2 powders were mixed according to the stoichiometry of (Dy0.25Tm0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7, ball milled for 24 h in a Si3N4 jar with Si3N4 balls and ethanol solution, dried at 60 °C for 24 h, passed through a 120-mesh sieve, and then synthesized by pressure-less synthesis at 1550 °C for 6 h.
Process_Text.simplified: Stoichiometric rare-earth oxide plus SiO2 mixture, 24 h ball milling in Si3N4 jar/balls with ethanol, dried at 60 °C for 24 h, sieved through 120 mesh, then pressure-less synthesized at 1550 °C for 6 h.

Process_Info.Equipment: Si3N4 jar and Si3N4 balls; X-ray diffractometer D/max-2400 (Rigaku, Tokyo, Japan); SEM SUPRA 35 (Zeiss, Oberkochen, Germany) with INCAx-sight EDS

Microstructure_Text.original: All the detected peaks for the (Dy0.25Tm0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7 sample could be indexed to β-Yb2Si2O7. The homogeneous distribution of the RE elements is further confirmed by the SEM-EDS analysis. These observations illustrate that the as-synthesized powders are pure single-phase β-(Dy0.25Tm0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7 solid solutions.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: Pure single-phase β-type disilicate with homogeneous RE distribution.

Properties_Info.Test_Condition: Room-temperature XRD phase identification after powder synthesis at 1550 °C for 6 h
Properties_Info.Note: Reported as pure single-phase β solid solution.

Composition_Info.Note: SEM-EDS point analysis on the hot-pressed bulk sample gave RE ratio Dy0.26Tm0.26Yb0.24Lu0.24.

Process_Text.original: Rare-earth oxides and SiO2 powders were mixed according to the stoichiometry of (Dy0.25Tm0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7, ball milled for 24 h in a Si3N4 jar with Si3N4 balls and ethanol solution, dried at 60 °C for 24 h, passed through a 120-mesh sieve, synthesized by pressure-less synthesis, and then hot-pressed in a BN-coated graphite mold at 1860 °C under 30 MPa to fabricate the bulk sample.
Process_Text.simplified: Stoichiometric powder processing followed by hot pressing in BN-coated graphite mold at 1860 °C under 30 MPa to obtain bulk β-phase material.

Process_Info.Equipment: Si3N4 jar and Si3N4 balls; BN-coated graphite mold; X-ray diffractometer D/max-2400 (Rigaku, Tokyo, Japan); SEM SUPRA 35 (Zeiss, Oberkochen, Germany) with INCAx-sight EDS

Microstructure_Text.original: The corresponding hot-pressed bulk material is also pure single-phase β-(Dy0.25Tm0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7 solid solution. SEM-EDS point analysis gave the atomic ratio Dy:Tm:Yb:Lu nearly 1:1:1:1.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: Hot-pressed bulk remained pure single-phase β with nearly equimolar RE distribution.

Properties_Info.Test_Condition: Room-temperature XRD phase identification after hot pressing at 1860 °C
Properties_Info.Note: Reported as pure single-phase β solid solution.

Composition_Info.Note: As-synthesized powder at 1550 °C contained mixed β and γ phases.

Process_Text.original: Commercial rare-earth oxides and SiO2 powders were mixed according to the stoichiometry of (Dy0.25Ho0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7, ball milled for 24 h in a Si3N4 jar with Si3N4 balls and ethanol solution, dried at 60 °C for 24 h, passed through a 120-mesh sieve, and then synthesized by pressure-less synthesis at 1550 °C for 6 h.
Process_Text.simplified: Stoichiometric oxide mixture processed by 24 h ball milling, drying, sieving, and pressure-less synthesis at 1550 °C for 6 h.

Process_Info.Equipment: Si3N4 jar and Si3N4 balls; X-ray diffractometer D/max-2400 (Rigaku, Tokyo, Japan); GSAS for Rietveld refinement

Microstructure_Text.original: The powders synthesized at 1550 °C contain a dual-phase mixture of β-type solid solution as major phase, together with a decent amount of γ-type solid solution. Quantitative phase analysis based on the Rietveld method shows that the β-phase accounts for 61.15 wt% in the mixture, whereas the γ-phase accounts for 38.85 wt%.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: 1550 °C powder is a β + γ dual-phase mixture, with β as the major phase.

Properties_Info.Test_Condition: Room-temperature Rietveld refinement of as-synthesized powder after 1550 °C synthesis
Room-temperature Rietveld refinement of as-synthesized powder after 1550 °C synthesis

Measured_Composition.Measurement_Method: SEM-EDS point analysis and TEM-EDS mapping

Composition_Info.Note: SEM-EDS point analysis for both β and γ phases in the 1650 °C hot-pressed bulk sample gave RE ratio approximately Dy0.27Ho0.26Yb0.25Lu0.22. TEM-EDS mapping confirmed atomic-scale compositional homogeneity of Dy, Ho, Yb, and Lu in both β and γ lattices.

Process_Text.original: Rare-earth oxides and SiO2 powders were mixed according to the stoichiometry of (Dy0.25Ho0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7, ball milled for 24 h in a Si3N4 jar with Si3N4 balls and ethanol solution, dried at 60 °C for 24 h, passed through a 120-mesh sieve, synthesized by pressure-less reaction, and then fabricated via hot-pressing sintering at 1650 °C under 30 MPa to produce the bulk sample used for XRD, SEM-EDS, and aberration-corrected STEM characterization.
Process_Text.simplified: Stoichiometric precursor powder followed by hot pressing at 1650 °C under 30 MPa; bulk sample characterized by XRD, SEM-EDS, and aberration-corrected STEM.

Process_Info.Equipment: Si3N4 jar and Si3N4 balls; BN-coated graphite mold; X-ray diffractometer D/max-2400 (Rigaku, Tokyo, Japan); SEM SUPRA 35 (Zeiss, Oberkochen, Germany); double aberration-corrected STEM Titan Themis Z (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, USA)

Microstructure_Text.original: Fabricating the sample via hot-pressing sintering method at 1650 °C results in decreased amount of β-phase down to 33.16 wt%, compensated by increased amount of γ-phase up to 66.84 wt%. Both β-phase and γ-phase in the 1650 °C hot-pressed bulk samples exhibit homogeneous RE elemental distributions. Aberration-corrected STEM resolved phase 1 as β-(Dy0.25Ho0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7 in the [112] zone axis and phase 2 as γ-(Dy0.25Ho0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7 in the [100] zone axis; atomic-resolution EDS maps directly visualized compositional homogeneity of Dy, Ho, Yb and Lu on the lattices of both phases.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: 1650 °C hot-pressed bulk is a γ-major mixed β + γ material. Both polymorphs are chemically homogeneous at SEM/TEM scales.

Properties_Info.Test_Condition: Room-temperature Rietveld refinement of bulk sample hot-pressed at 1650 °C
Room-temperature Rietveld refinement of bulk sample hot-pressed at 1650 °C

Microstructure_Text.original: Both the as-synthesized powders and the hot-pressed bulk material are mixtures of β-type and G-type disilicates. Quantitative phase analysis further reveals that the as-synthesized powders contain G-phase in 72.60 wt% and β-phase in 27.40 wt%, respectively.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: As-synthesized powder is a G-major β + G mixed material.

Composition_Info.Note: Phase-separated bulk sample showed obvious elemental segregation. SEM-EDS gave β-phase RE ratio La0.05Ce0.06Yb0.43Lu0.46 and G-phase RE ratio La0.35Ce0.35Yb0.16Lu0.14. The β-phase is enriched in Yb and Lu, whereas the G-phase is enriched in La and Ce.

Process_Text.original: Rare-earth oxides and SiO2 powders were mixed according to the stoichiometry of (La0.25Ce0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7, ball milled for 24 h in a Si3N4 jar with Si3N4 balls and ethanol solution, dried at 60 °C for 24 h, passed through a 120-mesh sieve, and then hot-pressed at 1650 °C for 2 h under 30 MPa in a BN-coated graphite mold.
Process_Text.simplified: Stoichiometric precursor followed by hot pressing at 1650 °C for 2 h under 30 MPa.

Process_Info.Equipment: Si3N4 jar and Si3N4 balls; BN-coated graphite mold; X-ray diffractometer D/max-2400 (Rigaku, Tokyo, Japan); SEM SUPRA 35 (Zeiss, Oberkochen, Germany); double aberration-corrected STEM Titan Themis Z (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, USA)

Microstructure_Text.original: The phase composition remains almost unchanged after hot-pressed at 1650 °C for 2 h, with G-phase in 72.15 wt% and β-phase in 27.85 wt%. SEM-EDS analysis shows obvious elemental segregation in both phases, i.e., the β-phase is enriched with Yb and Lu elements, whereas the G-phase is enriched with La and Ce elements. STEM and atomic-resolution EDS maps confirm compositional uniformity of La, Ce, Yb and Lu within each β and G lattice despite their non-stoichiometric distributions in different phases.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: 1650 °C bulk remains a G-major β + G mixed material with strong phase segregation: β enriched in Yb/Lu and G enriched in La/Ce.

Properties_Info.Test_Condition: Room-temperature Rietveld refinement of hot-pressed bulk sample at 1650 °C for 2 h
Room-temperature Rietveld refinement of hot-pressed bulk sample at 1650 °C for 2 h

Composition_Info.Note: Theoretical high-throughput DFT ensemble for β polymorph.

Process_Text.original: The configuration ensemble of β-(Dy0.25Tm0.25Yb0.25Lu0.25)2Si2O7 was constructed using stochastically generated special quasirandom structures. Supercells with 88 lattice sites were used. For the β-type structures, 558 unique configurations were included. DFT calculations were performed using VASP with the PAW method, PBE-GGA functional, 600 eV plane-wave cutoff, and a Gamma-centered Monkhorst-Pack k-mesh in the resolution of 2π × 0.03 Å−1.
Process_Text.simplified: β-phase SQS/DFT ensemble with 88-site supercells and 558 unique configurations, calculated by VASP-PAW-PBE at 600 eV.

Microstructure_Text.original: A hypothetically constructed β-type ensemble with randomized occupations of Dy, Tm, Yb and Lu on the RE sublattice was used to calculate the mixing-energy distribution and configurational entropy of mixing.
Microstructure_Text.simplified: Randomized β-phase configurational ensemble on RE sites.

Properties_Info.Test_Condition: Gaussian fitting of DFT mixing-energy distribution for β-type ensemble
Calculated from RE3+ cationic radii for β-type ensemble
